verdict.rationale: Render documents real sandbox isolation, not a dry-run. Every change or pull request gets an ephemeral preview copy of the full application stack, non-production environments can be blocked from reaching production services, and short-lived instances can run commands without connecting to production. Render's own article frames preview environments as agent sandboxes. Missing for 10: detail on how preview datastores are provisioned or seeded separately from production data, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Iterate quickly with ephemeral previews of your entire application architecture for every change.
every pull request gets its own running copy of the application stack.
Prevent non-production environments from accessing production services.
You can start a short-lived instance of your service to inspect its runtime or run one-off commands without connecting to production.
